newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on crop weather, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on crop weather, technicals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a forecast for warmer-than-normal weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
The market dropped despite news that frost damaged some of the corn and soy crop in southern Minnesota and northern Iowa.

"There was talk of some frost damage but the market wasn't too concerned about it. Also seasonally it's difficult to sustain a rally with cash coming into the pipeline," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was cited as a bearish market factor.
The NWS said above normal temperatures and below normal rainfall was expected in most of the U.S. Midwest from September 19 through September 23.

Chilly weekend weather may have hurt a minimal amount of corn in the northern Midwest, market sources said. Agronomists said frost early Saturday morning damaged corn and soybeans in some low-lying fields in northern Iowa and southern Minnesota.
Corn closed unchanged to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with Septmember down 4-3/4 at $3.57.
Corn dropped on fund and commercial selling with the fund selling totaling at least 10.0 million bushels, they said.
Commercial selling centered on Cargill Inc's sale of seven million bushels of December, the traders said.
The technical selling started at the opening because of the spillover from Sunday night trading which left December below chart support at $3.20 per bushel.
Late technical selling was noted at the $3.14-1/2 per bushel mark but the December contract started to recover on short covering and ended at $3.14-1/2, down seven cents.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 75,000 contracts, up from 70,339 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Smith Barney bought 1,000 December $3.40 calls at 5 to 5-1/4 cents and Cargill Investor Services bought 2,000 March $2.70 puts at 7/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, down from 27,440 contracts Friday.
